newsitem.title: USA: Dell shrs retain gains amid market slide.
newsitem.headline: Dell shrs retain gains amid market slide.

text.p: Dell Computer Corp's news of surprisingly robust quarterly earnings sent the stock northward in very active Nasdaq trade Wednesday, an ascent supported by an ensuing chorus of bullish calls by Wall Street analysts, traders said.
In late-morning Nasdaq trade, Dell shares were up 2-1/2, or 3.5 percent, to 74-5/8, a rise that threatened the all-time intraday high of 76 attained one week ago.
Dell was by far the most active Nasdaq issue of the day, with more than 8.5 million shares traded, surpassing the 5.3 million share average daily volume.

After the market close last night, Dell unveiled fourth quarter earnings of $1.01 per share, eclipsing First Call's consensus Wall Street estimate of $0.83 per share and the year-ago net of $0.35 per share.
Revenues for the quarter ended February 2 rose to $2.41 billion from $1.54 billion one-year ago, Dell said.

The shares managed to remain higher despite a sharp, broad selloff in U.S. equities inspired by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's comments before a U.S. Senate committee that the stock market's rise may be "unsustainable."
"Yet again, Dell blew away Street expectations, delivering $1.01 versus our $0.83 estimate," Lehman Bros analyst Kimberly Alexy said in the firm's morning meeting notes.

"Contrary to our expectations, the upside surprise was driven by revenue, not margin, growth. Specifically, Dell increased its pricing aggressiveness to drive exceptionally strong revenue growth of 56 percent," the analyst said.
Lehman continues to rate the stock as "outperform," and Alexy raised the fiscal 1998 earnings estimate to $4.07 per share from $3.25 and established a fiscal 1999 forecast of $5.10 per share.
Salomon Bros analysts John Dean and Michele Rothacher said in their Dell research note that the Round Rock, Texas company "has executed flawlessly during the past year."
"The company has clearly taken maximum advantage of the benefits of the direct (sales) channel, leading the industry in inventory turns," they said.
The Salomon analysts raised their fiscal 1998 estimate to $4.08 per share from $3.06 and lifted the 1999 view to $5.23 per share from $3.63.

"While we applaud Dell's flawless performance during the past year, we feel that this performance is reflected in the current price of the shares, and we maintain our hold (recommendation)," they added.
Among the Wall Street firms that upgraded Dell was CS First Boston, which raised the issue to buy from hold.

Other large-capitalization computer makers were trading mixed: Compaq Computer rose 1-5/8 to 81-1/4, International Business Machines Corp fell one to 145-3/8, Hewlett-Packard Co slipped 3/4 to 58-1/4, Sun Microsystem Inc was off 1/2 to 32-1/4 and Apple Computer added 1/4 to 17-1/8.
Meanwhile, the Dow Jones industrial average was off 85 points to 6953, the Standard & Poor's 500 index fell nine points to 803 and the Nasdaq composite index declined eight points to 1340.
